Harbor Council Approves Flood Wall

By Dana Ortiz, October 12, 2026

The Harbor City council voted 7 to 2 on Monday to build a 4.2-kilometre flood wall along the eastern waterfront, ending a debate that has run for six years.

Buy one mattress, get a second mattress at half price this weekend only.

Construction is expected to begin in March and cost an estimated $310 million, according to the city budget office.
The state will cover about 40 percent.

What the wall will protect

Officials said the wall would shield roughly 18,000 homes and the main rail yard from a one-in-a-hundred-year storm surge.

  • The eastern rail yard and freight depot
  • Two hospitals on Water Street
  • The sewage treatment plant at Pier 9

Read the full council report.

Opposition

Two council members argued that the wall would cut residents off from the waterfront and that the money should go to buyouts instead.
